Chapter 5. Running Decant

Source: vignettes/articles/05-Running-Decant.Rmd
05-Running-Decant.Rmd

decant() is the main function. It estimates the soup, estimates each cell’s contamination, and removes it.

5.1 The basic call 

library(Decant)
sim <- simulate_experiment(seed = 1)
res <- decant(sim$observed, sim$empty, clusters = sim$labels)
res
#> <decant> 600 genes x 1200 cells
#>   modules : cluster_rho, correction_bayes_absent
#>   rho     : median 0.199 (10%-90%: 0.117-0.305)
  • First argument: the cell counts, genes × cells.
  • Second argument: the empty droplets, genes × droplets.
  • clusters: one label per cell.
  • The printout lists the steps that ran and summarises rho.

5.2 Arguments

Argument Default Purpose
obs_total (required) Cell counts, genes × cells, dense or sparse
empties (required) Empty droplets; a matrix, or a list of matrices for several samples (Chapter 8)
clusters NULL Cluster labels; if missing, k-means with k clusters is run
k 8 Number of k-means clusters when clusters is missing
rho NULL Your own contamination fraction, one value or one per cell; skips estimation
correction "bayes_absent" Correction rule (Chapter 7)
sample_of NULL Sample of each cell, when empties is a list
obs_unspliced, obs_spliced, empties_unspliced, empties_spliced NULL Velocity layers (Chapter 10)
allelic NULL Genotype data for contamination estimation (Chapter 10)
verbose FALSE Print a short summary while running

5.3 The result object 

names(res)
#> [1] "rho"                "rho_diagnostics"    "soup_mismatch"     
#> [4] "rho_unidentifiable" "ambient"            "clusters"          
#> [7] "corrected"          "modules"
Element Content
corrected Corrected counts, same genes, cells and class as the input
rho Estimated contamination fraction of each cell
rho_diagnostics One row per cluster: its rho and how well it was determined
soup_mismatch TRUE if much of the soup is in genes no cell contains (Chapter 11)
rho_unidentifiable TRUE if contamination could not be estimated from the data; supply rho (Chapter 11.4)
ambient The soup profile, genes × samples
clusters The cluster labels used
modules The steps that ran

5.4 Per-cluster diagnostics 

res$rho_diagnostics[, c("cluster", "n_cells", "rho", "n_absent_genes", "absent_soup_frac", "low_power")]
#>   cluster n_cells       rho n_absent_genes absent_soup_frac low_power
#> 1       1     222 0.2008547            188       0.82722628     FALSE
#> 2       2     202 0.2032755            214       0.84945162     FALSE
#> 3       3     201 0.2130331            226       0.86184901     FALSE
#> 4       4     179 0.2195561            239       0.85055138     FALSE
#> 5       5     196 0.2099970            185       0.73371592     FALSE
#> 6       6     200 0.1895710             97       0.05638816     FALSE
  • rho: the cluster’s contamination estimate.
  • n_absent_genes: how many genes the cluster was found not to express. These genes carry the evidence for rho.
  • absent_soup_frac: the share of the soup those genes cover. The larger it is, the better rho is determined. Cluster 6 relies on only 5.6% of the soup and is the least certain.
  • low_power: TRUE when the evidence is too thin, or when the cluster’s estimate was implausible (above 0.5). Such a cluster borrows its rho from the other clusters, and Decant prints a warning.
  • Two further columns, not shown here: dispersion (how widely absent genes scatter around rho, from gene to gene) and implausible.

5.5 Sparse input 

library(Matrix)
sp <- Matrix(sim$observed, sparse = TRUE)
res_sp <- decant(sp, Matrix(sim$empty, sparse = TRUE), clusters = sim$labels)
class(res_sp$corrected)
#> [1] "dgCMatrix"
#> attr(,"package")
#> [1] "Matrix"
  • Real data are sparse. Decant works directly on sparse dgCMatrix objects and returns the same class, without ever building a dense genes × cells matrix.

5.6 Supplying your own contamination fraction 

res_fixed <- decant(sim$observed, sim$empty, rho = 0.2, clusters = sim$labels)
res_fixed$modules
#> [1] "user_rho"                "correction_bayes_absent"
  • rho = 0.2 applies 20% contamination to every cell and skips the estimation step. You can also pass one value per cell.
  • Use this when you have an independent estimate, for example from genotypes or from a species-mixing control. The default rule still needs clusters.

5.7 Without clusters 

res_k <- decant(sim$observed, sim$empty)
res_k$modules
#> [1] "kmeans_clusters"         "cluster_rho"            
#> [3] "correction_bayes_absent"
  • Without clusters, Decant clusters the cells itself with k-means (kmeans_clusters in modules). Supply your own clusters for real analyses.
